author: Rahul kp
topic: Sacrificing Ratio and Premium on Admission
title: Sacrificing Ratio
hook: who gives up, gets the premium!
simple_words: Old partners give up some profit share to the new partner, so they share his premium in that lost proportion.

definitions.meaning: Ratio in which old partners give up their share of profit in favour of the new partner. It is found as old share minus new share.
definitions.note: Not the same as the new ratio!

definitions.meaning: Amount the new partner brings, over his capital, for the right to share in the firm's existing goodwill. Old partners receive it.

key_points: Sacrifice of each old partner = ==Old share − New share==.
If the question is silent, assume the new partner takes his share from old partners in their old ratio.
Premium is shared by old partners in the ==sacrificing ratio==, not in the new ratio.
!!Do not use the old ratio for premium unless the sacrifice is in the old ratio or the question says so.!!

formulas.name: Sacrifice of an old partner
formulas.legend: Old share = share before admission. New share = share after admission. A negative answer means the partner gains.

formulas.name: New partner's goodwill share
formulas.rhs: Goodwill of firm × New partner's share
formulas.legend: Goodwill = value of firm's goodwill. New partner's share = fraction he gets. Premium is split in the sacrificing ratio.

insight.text: The partner who gives up more profit share receives more of the premium.

memory_trick.explanation: Always subtract the new share from the old share. Think of a pizza: the slice you lose is what you had minus what you now hold.

steps: Write old shares of all partners
Fix new shares of old partners
exam_tip: Check the question wording on how the new share is taken. It decides the sacrificing ratio, so read it before calculating.

doubt.question: Why not share the premium in the new ratio?
doubt.answer: Premium compensates for profit share lost. Only the loss, which is the sacrifice, matters. The new ratio shows future profit sharing, not what was given up.

mistakes.wrong: Sharing the premium in the new profit-sharing ratio
mistakes.right: Share it among old partners in the sacrificing ratio.

mistakes.wrong: Calculating sacrifice as New share − Old share
mistakes.right: Sacrifice = Old share − New share. A negative result means a gain.

mistakes.wrong: Crediting the premium to the new partner's capital account
mistakes.right: Credit the old partners' capital accounts in the sacrificing ratio.

mistakes.wrong: Always using the old ratio to divide the premium
mistakes.right: Use the old ratio only if sacrifice is in the old ratio or the question says so.
